textual.context: Presented as a promotional step-by-step tutorial. The description claims the speaker found a website that worked, while the source records do not independently verify that claim.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised game-asset benefit is directly linked to visiting an external destination, submitting a username, selecting device information, and requesting an amount, which may require later assessment of the destination and transaction flow.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether the website delivered UC or Battle Points, what happened to the entered username, or whether any transaction occurred.

textual.observation: The promoted process may require downloading one or more apps as a bot-verification step before receiving the requested UC and Battle Points.

textual.limitations: The records do not identify the apps, their permissions or behavior, whether downloading them was mandatory, or whether the reward was provided.

visual.observation: A PUBG-themed webpage visibly promotes “Get Free UC & Battle Points” and shows an “Account Info” form requesting a PUBG username and a device selection; the phone display shows “Android” selected.
visual.context: The request appears within a promotional webpage demonstration; the supplied frames do not establish whether the page is official or independently operated.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised in-game reward is linked to submitting an account username and device information, creating a task-relevant reward-and-data-request relationship.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show whether credentials beyond a username are requested, whether any information is submitted successfully, or whether the promised UC or Battle Points are delivered.

visual.observation: After an amount-selection and generation sequence showing “55000 BP,” the webpage displays a “Premium Content / Lock” screen instructing the viewer to download two free apps and perform actions for 30 seconds to unlock the added rewards; subsequent frames show a Google Play listing and gameplay screens.
visual.context: The sequence is presented as part of the same promotional webpage flow, with the required app activity shown through Google Play and installed-app/game screens.
visual.potential_relevance: Access to the promised PUBG-related reward is conditioned on downloading multiple apps and completing specified activities, linking a substantial reward claim to an unusual third-party offerwall task.
visual.limitations: The sparse samples do not establish whether the apps were actually installed, whether the required actions were completed, whether permissions or payment details were requested, or whether any reward was unlocked.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes free PUBG Mobile UC and Battle Points through an external website that asks viewers to enter a username, choose a device, and select an amount. The reward flow requires app downloads or offer completion and includes a locked-reward screen with a bot-verification instruction. These combined actions support a deceptive solicitation, without establishing whether apps were installed, information was misused, or rewards were delivered.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The content presents an explicit purported bypass for obtaining PUBG Mobile assets without ordinary acquisition: viewers are directed to an external website, asked to enter a username and device, select an amount, and proceed through a locked app-offer flow to obtain free UC and Battle Points. The evidence does not establish that the bypass worked or that the assets were delivered.
